proposals.name: Compact complete payoff
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the joke is very brief yet fully understandable and delivers a complete payoff; score 0 when it is incomplete, padded, or requires substantial missing context.
proposals.rationale: R11, R12, and R46 achieve recognizable premises and payoffs with exceptional compression, unlike the extended explanations in R32 and R39.

proposals.name: Conversational naturalness
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the wording resembles a plausible spontaneous exchange or thought; score 0 when the setup feels mechanically assembled or unnatural.
proposals.rationale: R03 and R10 use believable domestic dialogue and reactions, whereas R06 and R32 foreground contrived setups.

proposals.name: Semantic reframe
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a final word or phrase sharply changes how an earlier statement is understood while remaining coherent; score 0 when no reinterpretation occurs.
proposals.rationale: R41 and R46 both make an earlier idea snap into a new literal interpretation, while many card-favored puns merely substitute a similar-sounding word.

proposals.name: Specific absurd detail
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when an unusual, concrete detail creates a vivid comic image and materially strengthens the payoff; score 0 when the joke uses only generic or abstract wording.
proposals.rationale: R23 and R56 use highly specific details—multiple restaurant birthdays and a bizarre cucumber water pistol—to create distinctive comic imagery.

proposals.name: Reference repurposing
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a familiar song, text, person, or cultural reference is transformed into a new comic mechanism; score 0 when it is merely mentioned without transformation.
proposals.rationale: R03 repurposes song lyrics, R18 reworks chemistry terminology, and R45 converts Sartre into a dating-service premise.

proposals.name: Pointed platform meta-humor
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when self-reference to a forum or online behavior exposes a specific contradiction or recognizable practice; score 0 when the platform reference is generic or decorative.
proposals.rationale: R13, R30, R44, and R52 make targeted observations about joke forums, reposting, blocking, or commenting, while R48 is largely a generic platform plea.

proposals.name: Self-undermining irony
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the speaker’s stated attitude is contradicted by their own behavior or wording in a precise, revealing way; score 0 when no meaningful contradiction exists.
proposals.rationale: R10 turns a warning into encouragement, and R19 calls the speaker terrible while openly presenting the allegedly questionable behavior.

proposals.name: Sound-alike transformation
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when reading aloud reveals a clear, intelligible phonetic transformation that carries the joke; score 0 when the sound relation is absent or too distorted to recognize.
proposals.rationale: R16, R29, R39, R50, and R53 all depend heavily on spoken sound patterns, a feature that can be overvalued without judging how naturally the transformation lands.

proposals.name: Exact orthographic pun
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when spelling or word segmentation supports two clean readings that are both relevant; score 0 when the spelling trick is forced, misspelled, or relevant to only one reading.
proposals.rationale: R04, R05, R35, and R47 present explicit written puns, illustrating a surface feature that can receive credit even when the broader joke is thin.

proposals.name: Premise-punchline fit
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the punchline directly answers, extends, or resolves the setup; score 0 when it could be attached to almost any setup.
proposals.rationale: R17, R20, and R41 each make the payoff depend on the exact preceding premise, unlike interchangeable one-word puns such as R04 and R05.

proposals.name: Unexpected logical bridge
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the connection between two domains is initially surprising but becomes inevitable in retrospect; score 0 when it is either obvious or merely random.
proposals.rationale: R17 links relationships and algebra, R23 links birthdays to restaurant desserts, and R46 links hesitation to the name of an umbrella.

proposals.name: Pause and reveal timing
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when line breaks, pauses, or delayed wording control the reader’s expectation and make the reveal land cleanly; score 0 when presentation gives no usable timing or obscures the payoff.
proposals.rationale: R03, R10, and R41 use staged dialogue or spacing to delay and then reveal the key interpretation.

proposals.name: Controlled tonal collision
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when an ordinary, serious, or elevated frame collides with a sharply contrasting comic turn without losing clarity; score 0 when the tonal change is absent or merely jarring.
proposals.rationale: R20, R33, and R43 place bodily, historical, or religious material beside abrupt comic turns, revealing how tonal contrast can be mistaken for complete comedic construction.

proposals.name: Recognizable social observation
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the joke captures a specific, broadly recognizable behavior or institutional absurdity; score 0 when it contains no observation beyond a lexical trick.
proposals.rationale: R40, R44, and R49 comment specifically on politicians, subreddit blocking, and recommendation systems rather than relying solely on word substitution.

proposals.name: Inventive handling of taboo
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when sensitive material is paired with an original, precise comic mechanism; score 0 when shock, cruelty, or taboo reference is the primary source of humor.
proposals.rationale: R25, R33, R43, and R60 use controversial subjects with very different levels of comic construction, helping distinguish inventive framing from provocation alone.

proposals.name: Meta-disclaimer furniture
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text contain apologies, repost caveats, audience-directed disclaimers, or self-conscious posting language? Judge only visible presence; do not judge merit, originality, or humor.
proposals.rationale: Such furniture can attract attention or signal community positioning independently of comedic craft. It appears in the repost disclaimer of R08 and the self-effacing framing of R32.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission strategy and anticipated audience management

proposals.name: Practised delivery polish
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text show practiced control of setup length, reader guidance, punchline isolation, or dialogue staging? Judge only the extent of these traces, never whether the execution is good.
proposals.rationale: A practiced poster may know how to package text for rapid recognition, while practice may also improve genuine craft. R05 uses consistently staged dialogue, and R27 uses highly managed advertising-style framing.

proposals.name: Source-transfer residue
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the wording suggest transcription, translation, quotation, or transfer from a pre-existing joke source through canonical phrasing, awkward lexical choices, or excess explanation? Judge only the visible residue, not its quality.
proposals.rationale: Transferred material can carry familiarity or distribution advantages unrelated to the local writing, though source choice may also affect craft. R12 and R39 preserve nearly identical elaborate phrasing, while R44 has conspicuously formal translated-style wording.

proposals.name: Era-bound topical idiom
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text contain references, slang, technology, political language, or calendar markers that locate it in a particular forum era? Judge only temporal traceability, never whether the reference is effective.
proposals.rationale: Timing can make a text more immediately legible or socially salient without changing its underlying construction, while topical fit can also affect genuine reception. R21 names Clinton and Trump, and R26 explicitly invokes the end of a decade.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission timing and position in the entry stream

proposals.name: Retelling-chain cues
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text signal a first telling, repost, familiar template, deliberate repetition, or assumed knowledge of an earlier joke? Judge only the visible chain-position cues, not novelty or humor.
proposals.rationale: A joke's place in a circulation chain can affect familiarity and attention separately from local wording, though novelty may also matter to genuine reception. R08 explicitly discusses being a repost, and R40 repeats the same sentence as a repost-like device.

proposals.name: Taboo-register intensity
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text rely on sexual, scatological, violent, tragic, religiously inflammatory, or slur-adjacent material? Judge only the amount and explicitness of taboo content, never whether it is acceptable or funny.
proposals.rationale: Taboo material can trigger attention, discomfort, or uneven audience participation independently of craft, while taboo subject matter can also contribute to genuine reception. R14 uses suicide-vest imagery, and R51 combines bereavement with an aviation reference.
proposals.upstream_parent: audience taboo tolerance and social-climate effects

proposals.name: Orthographic irregularity
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text contain spelling errors, grammatical fragments, unusual capitalization, punctuation runs, repeated glyphs, or malformed layout? Judge only the extent of irregularity, never whether it improves the joke.
proposals.rationale: Visible noise can act as a strong textual cue for automated systems or reader attention without being a comedic property. R22 contains all-caps promotional-looking text and misspellings, while R60 contains multiple conspicuous spelling errors.

proposals.name: Platform-native self-reference
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text directly mention Reddit, subreddits, comments, apps, front pages, reposting, or other forum-native concepts? Judge only the density and explicitness of these references, never their quality.
proposals.rationale: Community references can create in-group visibility and affiliation independently of joke construction, though shared identity can also contribute to genuine reception. R06 centers the Reddit app, and R52 refers directly to blocking a subreddit and making Reddit great again.
proposals.upstream_parent: audience identity, following, and community affiliation

proposals.name: Stock-format reliance
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text commit to a recognizable stock delivery form such as a one-liner, question-answer, dialogue, riddle, lyric continuation, or extended narrative template? Judge only format presence, never whether the format works.
proposals.rationale: Format familiarity can make an item easy to process or classify independently of its local wording, while format can also be part of genuine comedic construction. R16 is a compact one-liner, whereas R44 uses an extended formal narrative setup and reveal.

proposals.name: Named-entity salience
proposals.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text depend on recognizable people, brands, places, religions, fictional characters, or institutions? Judge only the number and prominence of such entities, never their relevance or humor.
proposals.rationale: Named entities can supply familiarity, identity cues, or social attention independently of textual craft, though shared knowledge may also affect genuine reception. R04 uses a religiously loaded personal name, and R35 invokes Indiana Jones as a recognizable cultural anchor.

proposals.name: Late semantic reframe
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the setup invites an ordinary interpretation and the ending sharply forces a second interpretation; score 0 when no meaningful reinterpretation occurs.
proposals.rationale: This distinguishes compact reversals such as R07 and R27 from flatter constructions, helping explain why dense ranking may exceed criterion aggregation.

proposals.name: Phonetic transformation precision
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a spoken sound maps cleanly and recognizably onto a new phrase, with context supporting the mapping; score 0 when the resemblance is strained or unclear.
proposals.rationale: R37 and R56 use elaborate sound transformations, while R29 and R41 show less reliable phonetic or orthographic execution; this may explain scorecard over-crediting wordplay.

proposals.name: Platform-aware meta-fit
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a forum convention such as reposting, posting, or voting is itself converted into the punchline; score 0 when the platform reference is merely decorative.
proposals.rationale: R04, R12, R39, and R46 all invoke joke-forum behavior, but with very different degrees of comic integration, creating disagreement between text-sensitive and checklist-style judgments.

proposals.name: Cultural reference leverage
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a widely recognizable person, event, song, or phrase supplies an immediate premise that is meaningfully transformed; score 0 when the reference is obscure or only name-dropped.
proposals.rationale: R14, R45, R49, and R53 show culturally familiar material being used in different ways, while R34 and R59 illustrate references that can receive credit despite weaker transformation.

proposals.name: Concrete image specificity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when unusual, vivid details make the scenario instantly pictureable and directly support the comic turn; score 0 when the joke remains abstract or generic.
proposals.rationale: The cucumber-shaped water pistol in R06 and the 365 restaurant IDs in R15 provide unusually specific imagery; R27 and R50 offer contrasting examples of detail serving a premise.

proposals.name: Premise escalation
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the joke compounds a premise through successive developments and ends with its strongest escalation; score 0 when it makes one flat assertion without development.
proposals.rationale: R15, R22, and R50 build through multiple steps, whereas many short scorecard-favored puns do not; this interaction can be missed by additive criteria.

proposals.name: Conversational voice authenticity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the wording sounds like a spontaneous speaker with a distinct attitude, rhythm, and social perspective; score 0 when it sounds mechanically templated, padded, or disclaimer-heavy.
proposals.rationale: R09, R21, R39, and R51 derive much of their effect from an identifiable speakerly voice, a property that raw-text modeling may capture better than fixed formal criteria.

proposals.name: Self-undercutting confession
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the speaker’s own mistake, weakness, or contradiction unexpectedly defeats their stated intention; score 0 when the speaker is not personally implicated in the turn.
proposals.rationale: R21, R39, and R60 all make the narrator’s behavior the source of the reversal, while R09 similarly turns the speaker’s stated attitude against itself.

proposals.name: Idiomatic literalization
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a familiar expression is interpreted literally in a precise way that creates a strong contrast with its usual meaning; score 0 when the expression is used conventionally or the literal reading adds little.
proposals.rationale: R10, R27, and R44 literalize watch, views, and putting something on the record; this mechanism is distinct from generic pun presence and helps explain uneven model judgments.

proposals.name: Target-mechanism alignment
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the selected person, group, object, or setting is essential to the wordplay or premise and cannot be casually replaced; score 0 when the target is incidental.
proposals.rationale: R03, R25, R40, and R45 attach their mechanism to particular targets, whereas R34 and R59 show how topical targets can sometimes be present without equally strong structural necessity.

proposals.name: Constructed shock handling
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when taboo, hostile, sexual, or tragic material is paired with a precise reversal, absurdity, or wordplay mechanism; score 0 when provocation, cruelty, or shock is the main substance.
proposals.rationale: R25, R38, R45, and R59 contain potentially provocative material with varying levels of construction, helping identify cases where a scorecard may reward edginess more than comic workmanship.

proposals.name: Compression and payoff immediacy
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when every word contributes and the punchline is immediately legible without an explanatory tail; score 0 when the joke is padded, delayed, or requires extended unpacking.
proposals.rationale: R23 and R28 deliver compact turns, while R37 and R50 spend many lines reaching their mechanisms; disagreement may reflect dense sensitivity to payoff timing.

proposals.name: Orthographic delivery quality
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when spelling, grammar, formatting, and line breaks support the intended reading; score 0 when errors, spam-like text, or malformed presentation obstruct comprehension.
proposals.rationale: R36 is visually and linguistically corrupted, and R41 contains conspicuous errors; these contrast with otherwise understandable jokes whose textual surface is cleaner.

proposals.name: Freshness within a familiar form
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a recognizable joke template receives a specific, non-obvious twist; score 0 when it is a stock pun, direct repetition, or minimally altered repost.
proposals.rationale: R12, R23, R35, R46, and R55 use highly familiar forms, but only some add a fresh angle; this can explain scorecard enthusiasm for formal joke features despite weak novelty.

proposals.name: One-pass decoding accessibility
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when an average reader can recover the mechanism in one pass with one crisp inference; score 0 when multiple transformations, specialist knowledge, or explanation are required.
proposals.rationale: R08 and R44 are quickly decoded, whereas R22, R37, and R56 demand more layered interpretation; this helps explain why elaborate wordplay may be over-credited by the scorecard.

proposals.name: Forum-self-reference
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text mentions the subreddit, posting, comments, front pages, upvotes, or Reddit culture. Judge only visible presence; do not judge whether this feature is good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: These traces can track platform fluency and audience positioning rather than comic content. They may also reflect a practiced entrant who understands the venue, so the parent can partly affect genuine reader response. Examples: R06, R13, R23, R44.

proposals.name: Repost-chain disclosure
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text explicitly signals reposting, prior circulation, being a variant, or familiarity with an earlier joke. Judge only the textual signal; do not judge whether it is good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: Admissions of reposting or claims that nothing is new expose an item's place in a circulation chain. That can track familiarity and novelty expectations without measuring comic construction; adaptation can also affect genuine humor. Examples: R18, R27, R35.

proposals.name: Era-specific topical anchoring
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text contains dates, decade markers, contemporaneous politicians, public events, or other time-bound references. Judge only the amount of temporal anchoring; do not judge whether it is good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: Time-bound references reveal when an item belongs in the forum's stream and can track contemporaneous audience context rather than intrinsic joke quality. Topical fit can also affect genuine humor, so this is a mixed nuisance. Examples: R09, R15, R31, R46, R49.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission timing and position in the forum's historical stream

proposals.name: Engagement-bait furniture
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text uses click commands, download prompts, front-page appeals, upvote language, or SEO-like promotional phrasing. Judge only the presence of this furniture; do not judge whether it is good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: Promotional language can track visibility mechanics and distribution attempts independently of comic content. It is audience-management furniture rather than a property of the joke itself. Examples: R07, R13, R32, R42, R44.

proposals.name: Defensive posting furniture
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text contains apologies, disclaimers, self-justification, embarrassment, self-deprecation, or defensive asides about posting. Judge only the extent of these signals; do not judge whether they are good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: Such asides can track poster experience, community anxiety, and learned forum etiquette rather than joke quality. A practiced author may also write stronger material, so the upstream parent plausibly has a genuine-content pathway. Examples: R18, R26, R44, R51.
proposals.upstream_parent: author's practice and perceived community scrutiny

proposals.name: Source-like quotation register
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text displays extended quotation, formal citation, didactic exposition, source-like prose, or recitation of a stock passage. Judge only the visible source-like form; do not judge whether it is good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: Citation blocks, formal exposition, and near-duplicate recitations leave textual traces of transcription, translation, or lifting from established material. Provenance can track distribution history rather than comic quality, although source choice and adaptation can also affect genuine humor. Examples: R11, R35, R43, R53.

proposals.name: Editing and translation residue
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text shows typos, phonetic spellings, malformed spacing, missing punctuation, or inconsistent capitalization suggestive of rushed editing or language transfer. Judge only the visible residue; do not judge whether it is good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: Orthographic residue can track production workflow and surface friction without being a comic criterion. The conjectured parent is treated here as process noise, not as evidence about the joke's intrinsic quality. Examples: R03, R16, R19, R20, R32, R52.

proposals.name: Delivery-template commitment
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text commits to a recognizable delivery template such as dialogue, question-and-answer, narrative build, list, advertisement, lyric, or riddle. Judge only the format's extent; do not judge whether the format is good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: Repeated structural templates can track a poster's learned habits and familiarity with forum conventions rather than comic quality. Delivery format can nevertheless influence genuine humor, so this belongs in a sensitivity band. Examples: R10, R11, R23, R39, R42, R56.

proposals.name: Taboo-register intensity
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text invokes sexual content, bodily functions, religion, terrorism, death, violence, slurs, or other shock-adjacent subjects. Judge only the extent and explicitness; do not judge whether the feature is good, funny, tasteful, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: Taboo subject matter can track community boundaries and social circulation independently of craft. Because taboo framing can also alter genuine humorous response, the parent plausibly affects both nuisance behavior and comic reception. Examples: R08, R10, R12, R17, R25, R45, R58.

proposals.name: Performative typography cues
proposals.instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text uses read-aloud instructions, bold or italic emphasis, all caps, repeated punctuation, stage directions, lyric line breaks, or unusual spacing. Judge only the amount of performance cueing; do not judge whether it is good, funny, effective, or desirable.
proposals.rationale: These cues can track learned presentation habits and platform formatting conventions rather than comic quality. They may also influence delivery of the material, so their upstream parent could have a genuine-content pathway. Examples: R01, R05, R17, R32, R42, R60.

proposals.name: Phonetic phrase transformation
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a crisp sound-alike or spoken resegmentation makes an ordinary phrase suddenly fit; score 0 when no such transformation exists or it is unclear.
proposals.rationale: R02 and R40 use compact sound-based reinterpretations, while R29 shows how a similar device can become difficult to parse.

proposals.name: Polysemy with clean payoff
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a word’s distinct meanings are both clearly activated by the setup and payoff; score 0 when there is only a loose or accidental double meaning.
proposals.rationale: R21, R32, R53, and R54 each hinge on a word being read in two sharply different senses.

proposals.name: Delayed frame reversal
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the setup establishes one plausible interpretation and the final line sharply reinterprets it; score 0 when the ending adds no meaningful reversal.
proposals.rationale: R08, R47, and R57 build an initial situation whose final response changes how the preceding material is understood.

proposals.name: Premise-to-punchline causality
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the punchline follows naturally from a specific premise while remaining surprising; score 0 when the punchline is unrelated, arbitrary, or merely adjacent.
proposals.rationale: R07, R49, and R60 connect their endings directly to the stated subjects, whereas several card-high puns have weaker situational grounding.

proposals.name: Absurd concrete specificity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when unusual concrete details make the comic situation vivid and heighten its incongruity; score 0 when the joke remains generic or detail-free.
proposals.rationale: R03’s many birthday identities and R19’s bizarre water pistol provide memorable specifics; R50 similarly builds around a concrete public scene.

proposals.name: Platform-native self-reference
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the joke’s awareness of forums, posting, reposting, or readers is itself essential to the comic mechanism; score 0 when the platform reference is merely decorative.
proposals.rationale: R05, R10, R13, R25, R33, and R39 make the joke forum part of the premise rather than just its publication venue.

proposals.name: Reference transformed into mechanism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a recognizable cultural, literary, or fictional reference is actively reshaped into the punchline; score 0 when it is only named or quoted without transformation.
proposals.rationale: R04, R14, R36, and R55 integrate songs, scripture, philosophy, or superheroes into their central joke structures.

proposals.name: Taboo premise with comic conversion
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a sensitive or provocative premise is converted into a precise comedic mechanism; score 0 when it relies mainly on insult, shock, or taboo subject matter without a twist.
proposals.rationale: R06, R37, R41, and R44 show provocative premises whose effectiveness depends on whether a distinct mechanism accompanies the transgression.

proposals.name: Deliberate anti-joke structure
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when flat literalism, refusal of a conventional punchline, or deliberate undercutting clearly creates the joke; score 0 when the text is simply incomplete or non-comic.
proposals.rationale: R12, R16, R23, and R43 all approach anti-joke territory, making intentional flatness distinct from an absent payoff.

proposals.name: Standalone completeness
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the text supplies a coherent setup and a discernible ending without missing context; score 0 when it is fragmentary, incoherent, or stops before the payoff.
proposals.rationale: R15 and R35 are notably incomplete or malformed, while R23 illustrates how an apparently intentional blank can be hard to distinguish from missing content.

proposals.name: Surface readability
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when wording, spelling, and formatting make the comic mechanism immediately easy to follow; score 0 when errors or awkward construction substantially obscure it.
proposals.rationale: R09, R24, R29, and R51 contain wording or spelling problems that complicate otherwise recognizable pun structures.

proposals.name: Compression of comic information
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when every phrase efficiently advances the setup, misdirection, or payoff with no expendable material; score 0 when the text is bloated, repetitive, or lacks a developed mechanism.
proposals.rationale: R02, R05, R12, and R40 achieve their effects in very few words, while R39 demonstrates repetition without equivalent added development.

proposals.name: Expectation inversion
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the joke overturns a familiar expectation about a person, practice, or situation in a clear and surprising way; score 0 when it merely states a conventional association.
proposals.rationale: R22, R28, R30, and R60 all depend on reversing an ordinary social or practical assumption.

proposals.name: Dark consequence reframed
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a grim, sexual, or harmful consequence is introduced through a sharply specific reframing that creates comic distance; score 0 when darkness is presented without reframing or comic structure.
proposals.rationale: R11, R34, and R59 pair disturbing or embarrassing consequences with personal misdirection, illustrating a distinct form of dark comic construction.

proposals.name: Context-light accessibility
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the joke’s mechanism is understandable from the text with little specialized cultural or technical knowledge; score 0 when comprehension depends on obscure references or unexplained background.
proposals.rationale: R14, R16, R36, and R42 rely on scripture, literature, philosophy, or religious-calendar knowledge to make their mechanisms legible.

proposals.name: Length and elaboration
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much text bulk, preamble, lineation, or explanatory padding is present; judge extent only, never whether the joke is good or funny.
proposals.rationale: Length and layout bulk are stable lexical shortcuts. R01 and R30 use extensive framing or quotation, while R02 and R10 are highly compressed; bulk itself is not the comic mechanism.

proposals.name: Orthographic and layout noise
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for visible capitalization irregularities, spelling errors, punctuation runs, spacing anomalies, markdown emphasis, or unusual line breaks; judge extent only, never whether the joke is good.
proposals.rationale: Surface irregularities create conspicuous tokens independent of comic construction. R26 uses all-caps SEO-like wording, R58 contains multiple misspellings, and R03 uses lyric-style line breaks.

proposals.name: Practiced forum packaging
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for signs of habitual forum-oriented packaging, such as rapid openings, economical context, controlled setup, or a clearly isolated punch; judge only the visible practice signature, not its quality.
proposals.rationale: Repeated posting practice or editorial assistance can leave recognizable packaging habits. R25 uses a forum-aware meta setup, R43 stages a compact dialogue, and R44 opens with terse community-facing framing; these traces need not measure comic craft.

proposals.name: Source-transcription residue
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for visible signs that wording was quoted, translated, transcribed, or lifted from a pre-existing source; judge only the extent of source-like traces, never whether the joke is good.
proposals.rationale: Borrowed material can leave canonical wording, quotation blocks, lyrics, scripture, or mismatched register. R03 reproduces song lyrics, R30 quotes scripture at length, and R16 and R54 share near-identical inherited phrasing.

proposals.name: Audience-management furniture
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for apologies, repost caveats, self-abasement, edit notes, requests, content warnings, or instructions aimed at the forum audience; judge extent only, never whether these devices help the joke.
proposals.rationale: Posting logistics can be highly legible to a text model while remaining separate from the comic mechanism. R28 apologizes for reposting, R46 discusses reaching the front page, and R59 comments directly on its posting fate.

proposals.name: Delivery-template commitment
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for commitment to a stock delivery shell such as a question-answer riddle, difference joke, dialogue, narrative, or list; judge the format's presence only, never whether the format is effective.
proposals.rationale: Format habits are visible regardless of the underlying idea. R07 and R41 use difference or entrance shells, while R31 and R55 use question-answer turn-taking; the shell is a convention, not a quality judgment.

proposals.name: Taboo-register intensity
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for explicit sexual, scatological, bodily, violent, tragic, religious, political, or slur-adjacent material; judge only register intensity, never whether the material is funny.
proposals.rationale: Taboo vocabulary produces salient social and emotional cues that can attract shortcut behavior independently of craft. R21 and R22 invoke tragedy, R36 invokes sexual reproduction, and R45 uses sexualized religious imagery.

proposals.name: Era-coded forum idiom
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for vocabulary, current events, platform references, political slogans, or calendar markers that locate the text in a recognizable forum era; judge extent only, never whether the joke is good.
proposals.rationale: Historical placement leaves textual traces through changing platforms, slogans, and public figures. R33 uses subreddit and slogan language, R39 pairs Bernie with Clinton, and R60 contains an explicit decade marker; temporal visibility is not comic construction.

proposals.name: Retelling-chain self-awareness
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for framing that signals prior circulation or assumes familiarity with an existing joke, including repost notices, duplication, inherited wording, sequel language, or knowing repetition; judge extent only, never novelty or funniness.
proposals.rationale: A joke's place in a circulation chain can leave explicit repetition and provenance cues. R18 repeats its sentence verbatim, R28 calls itself a repost, and R50 describes itself as old to the subreddit.

proposals.name: Named-entity prerequisite density
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for reliance on proper names, brands, institutions, locations, quotations, or specialist concepts needed to parse the text; judge recognition demands only, never accessibility or quality.
proposals.rationale: Recognition prerequisites can proxy audience composition or cultural timing rather than comic construction. R10 uses atomic terminology, R19 combines dating brands with Sartre, and R31 depends on the LAX abbreviation.

proposals.name: Forum-self-reference fused to a real payoff
proposals.instruction: Score how much the joke's content points at the posting community itself (reposts, karma, comment culture, 'this sub') AND converts that reference into an actual comedic turn — a specific absurd consequence, an ironic reversal, or a punchline with substance. 10 = the self-reference is load-bearing setup for a twist that lands on its own (e.g., scripture quoted as evidence of prehistoric reposting; a specific book title delivered as the punchline). 5 = community reference present but the turn is generic. 0 = no self-reference, or self-reference that is only a complaint or plea with no turn at all.
proposals.rationale: A large dense-high cluster is forum-meta with a genuine payoff: R49 (Ecclesiastes framed as the original repost complaint), R15 (book-recommendation punchline), R46 (ironic upvote disclaimer), R57 (element puns inside a repost lament). Meanwhile R09 and R01 are forum complaints with no payoff and sit dense-low — the payoff, not the meta-ness, is what the scorecard's bank appears to miss.

proposals.name: Punchline the reader must construct
proposals.instruction: Score how much of the comedic mechanism is left unstated for the reader to assemble. 10 = the key link is never printed: a hidden compound the reader must merge, an implied answer to a posed comparison, or an unstated conclusion the framing forces; the 'aha' happens in the reader's head after a beat. 5 = partially stated, the reader finishes it. 0 = everything needed for the laugh is explicitly written out, or there is no mechanism.
proposals.rationale: R04 never prints 'umbrella' — the reader must combine the hesitation with 'brella'; R19 stops at '9 out of 10 suffered', leaving the tenth person's fate unsaid; R28 poses the difference question and stops. All are dense-high/card-low: a criteria bank judging 'is there a clear punchline?' likely marks these deficient, while the dense model treats the omission as the joke.

proposals.name: Freshness against the classic-joke canon
proposals.instruction: Using your general knowledge of widely circulated jokes, score how novel the construction is. 10 = you cannot place it in the standard bar/schoolyard/office canon; it feels authored for this post. 5 = a familiar formula carrying at least one genuinely new element. 0 = a canonical, decades-circulated joke reproduced nearly verbatim (famous pun setups, playground rhymes, stock bar riddles).
proposals.rationale: R03 and R37 are the same famous 'super-calloused fragile mystic hexed by halitosis' classic, R17 is the ancient 'Not on my watch' pun, and R47 is the schoolyard 'snot' rhyme — all card-high, dense-low. The dense model appears to perceive staleness of recognizable classics that explicit craft criteria (neat setup, clean pun) actually reward.

proposals.name: Transgression carried by craft, not shock
proposals.instruction: For jokes with taboo, mean, or dark premises, score whether the laugh mechanism works independently of the taboo. 10 = the actual turn is structural — a mundane detail, a subverted format, a pun or deadpan step that would still be funny with a neutral target. 5 = some mechanism but the shock does much of the work. 0 = naming the taboo or expressing hostility IS the entire payload.
proposals.rationale: Dense-high: R34 (self-help 'Step 1 / Step 2' format does the dark work), R26 (insult setup defused into 'Cashier'), R22 (genocide setup resolved by a bland middle name). Dense-low/card-high: R02 (burn the bar down — pure hostility), R11 ('gonna be the bomb' — stock shock pun), R59. The card seems to score edginess either uniformly up or down, missing the interaction.

proposals.name: Anticlimactic literalism played straight
proposals.instruction: Score whether the setup primes for an extraordinary or insulting reveal and the payoff is a flat, literally true, mundane answer delivered without winking. 10 = perfect bait-and-deflate: the mundane answer fully answers the question while letting all the air out. 5 = deflation present but the answer doesn't quite satisfy the setup. 0 = no bait-and-switch structure, or the payoff escalates instead of deflating.
proposals.rationale: R14 ('How much oil do Italians use?' — 'Olive oil'), R52 ('The Mountains blocked the view'), and R26 ('Cashier') are all dense-high/card-low. A scorecard judging 'strength of punchline' likely penalizes the flat answer, while the dense model registers the deadpan deflation itself as the pleasure.

proposals.name: Recognizable internet format, twisted
proposals.instruction: Score whether the joke's engine is faithful mimicry of a recognizable internet format (song-lyric meme block, app-launch pitch, clickbait headline, listicle, how-to) followed by a twist that exploits a convention of that format. 10 = the format replication is precise AND the twist depends on knowing the format. 5 = format present, twist generic to it. 0 = no recognizable format play.
proposals.rationale: R40 (a wedding vow that decodes into a rickroll — the lyric-block convention is the setup) and R38 (a startup-launch parody whose slogans invert Sartre) are dense-high/card-low. The payoff is format recognition plus betrayal, a mechanism a classical setup/punchline criterion bank has no slot for; R50 shows mere naming of a format ('Click bait.') without a twist scores low on this and sits dense-low.

proposals.name: Quasi-rational logic for an absurd scheme
proposals.instruction: Score first-person absurd plans on the internal logic the narrator supplies: concrete specifics, numbers, timing, cost-benefit framing that sounds sane while the plan is deranged, with the calm rationale as part of the joke. 10 = detailed, oddly plausible reasoning wholly in service of a lunatic goal. 5 = some specifics, thin logic. 0 = absurd claim asserted with no supporting reasoning, or no scheme present.
proposals.rationale: R12 (365 fake IDs itemized purely for free desserts, sealed with 'Just makes sense really') and R36 (the 11:55 timing and fence-height spec for a final 'shit post' of the decade) are dense-high. Contrast R29 (card-high, dense-low): the self-directed gag is asserted ('being really fucking ugly') with no engineered logic, so the card's 'has a twist' box ticks while the scheme-craft is absent.

proposals.name: Confessional micro-truth, specific not generic
proposals.instruction: Score first-person admissions of petty, near-universal human behavior. 10 = a behavior almost any reader recognizes in themselves, told with one concrete situational detail and a wry kicker, sounding like a true anecdote. 5 = recognizable but padded with generic self-labels. 0 = a bare generic self-insult ('I'm ugly', 'I'm terrible') with no depicted behavior, or no confession.
proposals.rationale: R53 (being told not to do something and immediately wanting it more, with believable dialogue) and R16 ('technically a repost… I'm a terrible person' — an honest micro-confession) are dense-high, while R29's generic 'I'm ugly' label is card-high/dense-low. The card appears to credit 'self-deprecation' as a category without distinguishing a specific depicted truth from a stock label.

proposals.name: Evergreen premise without a decaying news peg
proposals.instruction: Score the joke's independence from a specific news moment. 10 = fully intelligible and complete in any year; 5 = topical flavoring but the mechanism survives the news cycle; 0 = the joke collapses without knowing a particular election, scandal, storm, holiday coincidence, or date.
proposals.rationale: The card-high/dense-low side is thick with news-pegged items: R02 (2016 candidates), R51 (Lewinsky/Bernie), R11 (Eid on 9/11), R18 (Houston flooding). Dense-high items like R04, R35 and R49 need no calendar. The scorecard likely rewards 'topical reference' while the dense model discounts jokes welded to moments readers will age out of.

proposals.name: Pun load-bearing inside a working literal sentence
proposals.instruction: Score wordplay on double duty: the punning sentence must also function as a coherent, literally-true statement inside a real situation, so the pun is discovered rather than delivered. 10 = both readings fully make sense in context and the surface statement is worth saying on its own. 5 = the sentence limps on the literal level. 0 = a bare riddle-swap ('What do you call X?' '[pun word]') where nothing exists beyond the pun.
proposals.rationale: Dense-high: R35 ('I have no X and I know Y' works as a genuine complaint), R57 ('all the good ones Argon' inside a real forum lament), R04 (pun embedded in an invention anecdote). Card-high/dense-low: R43, R31, R13, R50 are bare substitution puns. The card's 'clever wordplay' criterion evidently can't distinguish embedded, load-bearing puns from free-standing swap puns.

proposals.name: Multiple independent payoffs, coherently stacked
proposals.instruction: Count distinct comedic turns the item delivers in its length, and score the stacking. 10 = three or more independent payoffs (e.g., name pun + slogan inversion + quote twist + format gag) that reinforce rather than crowd each other. 5 = two independent payoffs. 0 = one payoff, or payoffs that are just the same joke restated.
proposals.rationale: R38 stacks four turns: the app-name pun (Sartr), 'a relationship IS other people', the 'Commitment is an act, not a word' quote twist, and 'no end…to love!'. R57 stacks Neon + Argon + the repost lament; R40 stacks vow format + 'desert you' pun + lyric-meme recognition. All dense-high/card-low — a bank scoring 'a punchline' structurally misses density of turns.

proposals.name: Deadpan register held under absurd content
proposals.instruction: Score tonal control: how flat and unmarked the narration stays while the content is absurd or dark. 10 = completely straight prose — no caps, exclamations, or winking labels; the calm delivery is inseparable from the joke. 5 = mostly straight with one slip. 0 = the text signals its own outrageousness (shouting, 'EXTREMELY', fake-spelling gags, squealing asides), or nothing absurd to keep straight.
proposals.rationale: R34 (two calm self-help steps), R12 ('Just makes sense really') and R52's flat Q&A hold register perfectly and are dense-high. On the card-high side, R37 shouts ('EXTREMELY weak') and R20's joke is the shouted fake-German word itself — the card rewards the loud construction the dense model ranks low. Register is invisible to most explicit 'content' criteria.

proposals.name: Satire compressing a durable observation
proposals.instruction: For jokes about public life, score whether the line compresses a genuine, nameable irony (about power, media, addiction, or public behavior) that would still read as true years later. 10 = the observation is sharp and specific enough to stand alone as commentary. 5 = a real observation diluted by tribal framing. 0 = partisan cheer, insult, or a wish of harm with no perceivable twist or insight.
proposals.rationale: R45 ('People care when a comedian speaks') and R55 (blocking one sub 'made reddit great again' — slogan turned inward) compress actual observations and are dense-high; R02 and R05 express attitude with no twist and are card-high/dense-low. The card appears to credit 'political/topical' as a theme, missing that the mechanism — an observed irony — is what varies.

proposals.name: Bait-and-switch reveal that genuinely recontextualizes
proposals.instruction: Score twist structure on the quality of the second reading. 10 = the reveal forces you to re-read the setup with new meaning and was not foreseeable from the first clause. 5 = foreseeable but tidily executed, modest reframe. 0 = the 'twist' is the single most predictable dark completion of the setup, or the reveal adds no new frame to what was already stated.
proposals.rationale: R30 (onions/dad), R48 ('loves me not' / ruined flowers) and R41 ('she's still pregnant') are all card-high/dense-low: each reveal is the expected cheap-dark turn the setup primes. Dense-high items like R22 (a bland middle name that quietly reframes an entire biography) show the dense model rewarding recontextualization depth, which a generic 'surprise ending' criterion cannot grade.

proposals.name: Absurd imagery specified with payoff-feeding detail
proposals.instruction: Score bizarre images on precision-with-purpose. 10 = an absurd image built from concrete details where each detail later feeds the payoff — symbolically, phonetically, or logically — so nothing in the image is wasted. 5 = vivid absurdity with some decorative excess. 0 = generic weirdness, or no imagery at all.
proposals.rationale: R07's chase object (pink cucumber shape, water pistol, jello fill) is overloaded Freudian furniture that pays off in 'afreud', and R36's plan is specified with exactly the details (11:55, fence height, end of decade) the final pun needs; both out-perform their card ranks. A 'vivid language' criterion credits color, not the integration of each bizarre detail into the mechanism — which is what the dense model appears to register.

proposals.name: Venue-orientation: forum as subject and post furniture
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the text is oriented toward the host forum itself, either as subject matter (naming the forum, its subforums, moderators, users, karma or upvote mechanics, reposts, the 'front page', including jokes whose topic is the forum) or as commentary about this very post's prospects (apologies for reposting, appeals for attention, 'first post' or edit notes). 0 = no such orientation anywhere; 10 = the text is substantially about the forum or about its own posting. Judge only what is visibly written; do not judge whether the orientation is apt, polite or funny.
proposals.rationale: Modes 1 and 4. A joke that addresses the community about itself collects in-group recognition and reciprocity regardless of its construction, and a dense model trained on this venue's material can key on forum vocabulary as a proxy for community appeal. The slice is dense with it: R04 is nothing but a sentence about reposts stated twice; R29, R47 ('This joke won't get any upvotes...'), R48 (repost apology), R51 and R58 all spend their text on the venue or on their own posting rather than on a joke engine. Predictive of reception through address, not through comic craft.
proposals.upstream_parent: in-group audience capture and karma-management practice

proposals.name: Taboo and shock-content reliance
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the item's comic engine is carried by taboo material: sexual or scatological content, degradation of a person or group, atrocity or tragedy (terror attacks, the Holocaust, a parent's death), or slur-adjacent stereotype. 0 = no taboo content; 10 = the item is wholly built on shock. Extent of presence only; do not judge appropriateness, bravery, or funniness.
proposals.rationale: Mode 4 (register of taboo). Shock moves items through sensation and transgression-sharing, a circulation channel distinct from construction. The register cuts across both disagreement directions here, suggesting the models key on the register rather than craft: R02 (9/11 father) and R13 (Eid bomb) sit card-favored while R18 (Muhammed/followers) and R43 (Muslim Barbie) sit dense-favored, with R07 (Anne Frank) and R06 also in play. Taboo load is predictive but is not a joke-building property.
proposals.upstream_parent: circulation through shock and transgression culture

proposals.name: Named-politician and news-cycle anchoring
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how many distinct real-world public figures or datable news events the text names (politicians, scandals, elections, protests, storms, apps or memes tied to a specific news cycle), weighted by how central they are to understanding the item. 0 = no datable anchors; 10 = the item is unintelligible without them. Presence of anchoring only; do not judge the politics, the accuracy, or the joke.
proposals.rationale: Modes 2 and 3. Naming a politician or a storm taps partisan applause and a relevance window: reception tracks who was reading that week and whether they agreed, not how the joke is built. R09 (Hillary/Trump), R16 (Lewinsky/Bernie), R28 (White House garbage) and R46 (Houston 'making it rain') are all anchored this way and all sit card-favored, hinting the card's judges may read timeliness as substance. The anchor is a timing and audience-composition fingerprint, not a craft feature.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission timing within a news cycle and partisan audience alignment

proposals.name: Unintentional orthographic lapse density
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for the density of apparent unintentional errors: misspelled words, wrong short function words, missing sentence-initial capitals, missing terminal punctuation, and run-on strings with no punctuation. Exclude deliberate stylisation such as added ellipses, shouty capitals or meme spellings - count only what reads as error. 0 = clean text; 10 = error-riddled. Extent of error only; do not judge the writer beyond counting.
proposals.rationale: Mode 1. Lapses fingerprint a dashed-off one-off post or a long copy chain upstream of the item; whatever they correlate with, they are not properties of the joke's design. R14 carries 'areials' and 'recpetion' inside a decades-old pun, R05 has 'the' for 'they', R20 is a punctuation-less lowercase run-on, R27 lacks terminal punctuation, and R39's 'CHEAK' sits inside pasted-looking boilerplate. None of this bears on whether the underlying mechanism works.
proposals.upstream_parent: hasty one-off posting (casual or mobile entry)

proposals.name: Title, speaker labels, staged layout
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much reader-management scaffolding the text carries: a separate title or heading line, script-style speaker labels (BF:, Me:, You:), deliberate line-break stanzas marking beats, and markdown emphasis or italics used to stage a reveal. 0 = plain unformatted sentence or paragraph; 10 = title plus labelled dialogue plus staged line breaks. Layout presence only; do not judge whether the layout suits or helps the material.
proposals.rationale: Mode 4 (poster practice). Practised posters manage the reader with headings, labelled speakers and staged beats; the scaffolding predicts through presentation fluency and venue convention, not through the joke's idea, and the two models may key on it differently. R15 (title plus BF:/Me: script), R33 (title plus You:/Me:), R38 (title doing setup work), R22 (title plus an asterisked 'resume') and R60 (titled, paragraphed telling) show the fingerprint across both disagreement halves.
proposals.upstream_parent: author's practice in the format (habitual poster)

proposals.name: Performed-timing ellipses and hanging beats
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of transcribed spoken timing: strings of dots used as audible pauses ('...', '.....'), fragments deliberately left hanging mid-thought, and punch beats isolated on their own lines to imitate live delivery. Do not count titles or emphasis formatting. 0 = none; 10 = the text is dominated by dotted pauses and hanging beats. Presence of the device only; do not judge whether the timing is effective.
proposals.rationale: Mode 2. Dotted pauses and hanging beats are the fingerprint of a joke relayed from a live or recorded performer whose delivery the page cannot carry; a dense model can learn these marks as a proxy for the performer-sourced stratum. R03 ('...But he hesitated...'), R11 ('..... .....'), R19 ('... I don't have any Neons...') and R31's isolated lyric lines all cluster on the dense-favored side. The marks record sourcing, not construction.
proposals.upstream_parent: transcription of an external performer's spoken delivery

proposals.name: Chestnut reproduction: canonical punchline near-verbatim
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how closely the punchline mechanism reproduces a widely circulated, long-standing classic joke with little or no local adaptation - the setup-and-punch skeleton is one a general reader would likely have met before, nearly verbatim, merely re-anchored to new names. 0 = mechanism appears locally invented; 10 = near-verbatim canonical chestnut. Judge extent of reproduction only; do not judge whether the classic is good or deservedly famous.
proposals.rationale: Mode 3. Position in a retelling chain leaves a verbatim fingerprint: the same canonical punch appears twice in this slice - R34 (monk) and R60 (Gandhi) both land on 'super calloused fragile mystic hexed by halitosis' - and both sit card-favored, alongside R45 (Adam and Steve), R57 (mock-German bra) and R12 (Microsoft Word). Recognition and ritual re-telling drive reception here; the item's own contribution is a rename.
proposals.upstream_parent: position in the retelling chain of a circulating classic

proposals.name: Truncated delivery: setup without resolution
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how incomplete the joke's delivery structure is: a setup line with no resolution following it; a riddle, difference-question or 'what do you call' posed but never answered; a sentence cut off mid-delivery with the expected final line absent. 0 = complete structure with a resolution present; 10 = setup only, nothing that functions as a resolution. Structural completeness only; do not judge the quality of whatever is present.
proposals.rationale: Mode 2. Items mined or copied at scale sometimes lose their final line at a break; the fingerprint is a strangled structure, not a designed one. R54 is only 'A man phones his work and says', R10 poses a difference-question and never answers it, and R41 closes its setup with no discernible resolution line - all dense-favored, suggesting the dense model tolerates a stratum the card's judges penalise. This is a data-process artifact, orthogonal to any comic property.
proposals.upstream_parent: extraction or copy-paste pipeline truncating the source text

proposals.name: Self-explained punchline and appended gloss
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text explains its own mechanism: naming the figure of speech used, glossing the pun after landing it, appending a quotation or tagline that states the point, or telling the reader how to take what they just read. 0 = no self-annotation; 10 = the item extensively annotates its own point. Presence of self-explanation only; do not judge whether explaining helps or harms.
proposals.rationale: Mode 2. Second-hand texts gloss themselves for an audience the original never needed; the gloss fingerprints transmission, not the pun's construction. R40 names its own device ('That's a play on word'), R37 appends Ecclesiastes to state its point outright, and R32 appends a slogan and then explains 'Because a relationship IS other people!'. The annotation tracks sourcing and hand-holding; it is not itself comic material.
proposals.upstream_parent: relay or sourcing of the text from an external performer or joke list

proposals.name: Total word count band
proposals.instruction: Count the total words of the item text, including any title line, and map to the scale: 0 = 6 or fewer; 1 = 7-10; 2 = 11-15; 3 = 16-22; 4 = 23-30; 5 = 31-40; 6 = 41-55; 7 = 56-75; 8 = 76-100; 9 = 101-140; 10 = more than 140. Pure mechanical count; do not judge whether the length suits the material.
proposals.rationale: Mode 1. Length is the classic verbosity proxy: an end-to-end model can use raw extent as a proxy for strata (pasted quote-blocks, narrative builds) that have nothing to do with a joke's design. The slice spans from R35 and R47 at a handful of words to R37's pasted Bible quotation, R22's titled narrative and R60's paragraphed telling. Word count is predictive plumbing, not a property of comedy.

proposals.name: Community self-satire with crafted payoff
proposals.instruction: Judge whether the comic target is the joke-sharing community itself (reposting, lurking, commenting, hate-following, addiction) AND whether that self-reference carries a real constructed payoff rather than a bare mention. 10 = the community is unmistakably the butt and a crafted vehicle delivers the turn (a scripture passage repurposed as repost-lore; a book-title recommendation that lands the insult). 5 = community referenced but the turn is generic. 0 = no community self-reference, or a mention with nothing built on it.
proposals.rationale: R23 (dense 0.935 vs card 0.120) and R44 (0.897 vs 0.344) satirize repost culture through elaborate vehicles; R06, R18 and R58 do it more lightly and still rank dense-high. R54 shows the payload half matters: it gestures at the same community habit with no construction and sits dense-low (0.207).

proposals.name: Deliberately withheld punchline the reader supplies
proposals.instruction: Judge whether the item intentionally stops before the payoff so the reader completes it, with the gap itself carrying the comic charge. 10 = omission is clearly deliberate, the implied punchline is instantly reconstructible, and spelling it out would weaken the item (a difference-question asked and never answered; a closing rhetorical question left hanging; a claim left dangling unresolved). 5 = partial or ambiguous withholding. 0 = payoff fully explicit, or the cutoff reads like accidental truncation.
proposals.rationale: R28 (0.726 vs 0.259) asks a difference question and refuses the answer; R25 (0.838 vs 0.090) ends on a question the reader must answer about themselves; R34 (0.682 vs 0.125) rests entirely on a never-resolved claim. A rubric demanding an explicit punchline zeroes these; the dense signal does not.

proposals.name: Deadpan literal answer where wit expected
proposals.instruction: Judge whether an expectation of cleverness is set up and then answered with a flat, literal, or obvious reply played perfectly straight. 10 = the refusal to be clever is total and the mundanity is the laugh (the view was blocked by the mountains; the oil used is olive oil; the described person is simply the cashier). 5 = literal answer with a visible wink. 0 = figurative or witty punchline, or no expectation established.
proposals.rationale: R14 (0.872 vs 0.368), R55 (0.830 vs 0.203) and R32 (0.746 vs 0.213) are anti-jokes whose payoff is aggressive ordinariness. A scorecard keyed to punchline cleverness will underrate them, matching their low card percentiles while the dense model ranks them high.

proposals.name: Decode-depth of layered wordplay
proposals.instruction: Judge how much processing the wordplay demands and how many layers operate at once. 10 = the mechanism is hidden and must be reconstructed after a beat, or multiple puns stack, and re-reading rewards (a hesitation that inserts a syllable into a name; letters doing double duty as ex and why; element names serving as grammar). 5 = one non-obvious pun. 0 = a single immediate sound-alike swap, or no wordplay.
proposals.rationale: The dense model's top item, R29 (0.967 vs 0.176), requires reconstructing um+brella; R15 (0.898 vs 0.344) stacks X=ex and Y=why; R51 (0.805 vs 0.323) makes noble gases do grammatical work. Contrast R60 (dense 0.152) where Re:LAX decodes instantly: depth, not punning per se, separates the halves.

proposals.name: Taboo premise executed as absurdist incongruity
proposals.instruction: Judge whether the item courts a durable taboo (religion, atrocity, ideology, death) through its premise and executes with absurd juxtaposition or mundane flatness rather than by punning on the tragedy's mechanics, without dependence on any news cycle. 10 = the dare is structural and the laugh is incongruity (a prophet's career given as two bland steps; a modern middle name on a historical victim; a toy revealed as an inflatable). 5 = taboo present but carried by a stock pun. 0 = safe material throughout.
proposals.rationale: R17 (0.876 vs 0.159), R19 (0.790 vs 0.287), R40 (0.719 vs 0.139) and R26 (0.769 vs 0.090) are dense-high taboo dares with flat, absurdist delivery. The dense-low contrast cases pun directly on the atrocity's mechanism (R13 'gonna be the bomb', R52 'flying planes'), suggesting the card credits mere edginess while dense credits execution.

proposals.name: Sustained format parody with delayed breach
proposals.instruction: Judge whether the item inhabits a recognizable non-joke format (product pitch, app launch, news report, song lyric, how-to list) sincerely enough to establish it, then smuggles the payload through the format's own conventions. 10 = high fidelity with a late breach launched from inside the format (a pop lyric quoted as a solemn vow; ad copy in existentialist jargon; outbreak-report diction). 5 = format invoked but abandoned quickly or breached by an obvious one-word pun. 0 = plain narration, no mimicry.
proposals.rationale: R43 (0.803 vs 0.181) sustains a rickroll as a marriage vow, R37 (0.636 vs 0.165) writes dating-app copy in Sartre-speak, R56 (0.594 vs 0.124) mimics public-health reporting. R24 (0.379 vs 0.909) marks the boundary: it names the clickbait format and instantly breaches it with 'Click bait.' — nominal parody, dense-low.

proposals.name: Guilty self-recognition pursued shamelessly
proposals.instruction: Judge whether the item names a small, specific compulsion readers privately recognize in themselves and follows its logic without moral correction. 10 = recognition is instant and specific and the logic is pursued past respectability (wanting something more because it was forbidden; following a feed one despises; a 365-ID free-dessert scheme defended as common sense). 5 = relatable but generic or softened. 0 = no recognition target, or a corrective moral.
proposals.rationale: R57 (0.767 vs 0.054), R25 (0.838 vs 0.090) and R38 (0.786 vs 0.171) monetize recognition of the audience's own worst habits. R39 (0.237 vs 0.770) attempts relatable self-deprecation but the trait is generic, suggesting the card credits self-deprecation in general while dense credits specific, earned recognition.

proposals.name: Accurate knowledge substrate rewarding insiders
proposals.instruction: Judge whether a real factual or scholarly substrate (science, philosophy, scripture, etymology, mechanics) is load-bearing and accurate enough to delight knowledgeable readers while the joke still parses without it. 10 = substrate is structural and correct, and knowing it multiplies the joke (an existentialist dictum inverted into a slogan; noble-gas names as grammar; ion formation stated as fact; scripture quoted accurately). 5 = substrate present but decorative or half-remembered. 0 = no knowledge content.
proposals.rationale: R37 (0.636 vs 0.165), R51 (0.805 vs 0.323) and R36 (0.694 vs 0.132) run on correct niche knowledge, and R23 (0.935 vs 0.120) quotes Ecclesiastes accurately. The dense model consistently elevates items where prior knowledge is a multiplier — a property a generic rubric has trouble seeing.

proposals.name: High-low register collision as engine
proposals.instruction: Judge whether the item's central mechanism is a sustained collision between an elevated register (scripture, philosophy, technical, corporate) and low or trivial subject matter. 10 = the clash is structural and maintained end to end — solemn prose carrying absurd content (biblical cadence for repost lore; existentialist jargon for a hookup app; a publisher's title as insult). 5 = a momentary register slip. 0 = uniform register throughout.
proposals.rationale: R23, R37 and R44 (0.897 vs 0.344) each derive their force from tone-mixing and all sit dense-high. This is distinct from cleverness of content: the same content in flat diction would die, which is likely why a criterion bank keyed to content properties misses it.

proposals.name: Authentic confessional forum voice
proposals.instruction: Judge whether the item reads as a real individual's casual, self-aware admission in natural speech — first person, idiosyncratic detail, self-deprecating asides, believable dialogue — rather than recited joke inventory. 10 = a specific human voice with timing ('I know, I'm a terrible person'; a partner's protests quoted verbatim; a petty scheme narrated with pride). 5 = first person but template phrasing. 0 = anonymous third-person template diction.
proposals.rationale: The dense-high side is dense with voice: R06 (0.696 vs 0.112), R57 (0.767 vs 0.054), R34 (0.682 vs 0.125), R38 (0.786 vs 0.171). The dense-low side is dominated by recited templates (R09, R47, R59, R60), suggesting dense partly reads authenticity of voice that a structural rubric scores as zero.

proposals.name: Setup-payoff economy
proposals.instruction: Judge the ratio of buildup to payoff and whether every setup word works. 10 = minimal words, maximal turn — the payoff exceeds its buildup and there is no filler (a two-step instruction; a one-line reveal; a single conditional sentence). 0 = long, ornamented buildup whose payoff is a mild euphemism translation or a well-worn groaner that cannot repay the investment.
proposals.rationale: R17, R29 and R36 are dense-high with near-zero verbal fat. The mirror cases are R05 (0.272 vs 0.843), a paragraph of pseudo-technical ornament cashed out as a dishwashing euphemism, and R50 (0.075 vs 0.716), multi-clause biography for one worn pun — both card-high and dense-low, implying the card credits elaborate setups as craft while dense treats them as debt.

proposals.name: Punchline foreseeable from the setup alone
proposals.instruction: Simulate reading only the setup and predicting the punchline before seeing it. 10 = the exact punchline is callable in advance — the setup is effectively a label for its answer (questions about watches, weddings between antennas, airport email replies, turntable needles). 0 = the payoff could not be predicted, yet once read feels inevitable. Reverse-scored for quality: 10 means the reader finished the joke before the writer did.
proposals.rationale: R16 ('Not on my watch', 0.261 vs 0.811), R47 ('reception', 0.243 vs 0.896) and R60 (Re:LAX, 0.152 vs 0.742) are card-high and dense-low; in each, the setup gives the game away. The scorecard seems to reward tight setup-punchline fit, which here is indistinguishable from zero surprise.

proposals.name: Circulated-chestnut recognition
proposals.instruction: Judge how recognizable the punchline is as a long-circulated classic a broadly read judge has effectively met before. 10 = canonical, near-verbatim chestnut encountered many times (the super-calloused holy-man pun; 'it's snot'; the shift-of-wit chestnut; the stolen-Office 'you have my Word' chain). 5 = familiar construction, fresh wording. 0 = the construction feels authored for this item. Reverse-scored for quality: 10 signals staleness.
proposals.rationale: R12 (0.276 vs 0.734) and R50 (0.075 vs 0.716) are near-duplicate tellings of the same famous pun and the dense model dumps both while the scorecard rates both highly — the cleanest evidence in the slice that the card rewards structure the audience has already exhausted. R59 (0.123 vs 0.675) and R22 (0.502 vs 0.997) repeat the pattern.

proposals.name: Self-announcing or self-explaining frame
proposals.instruction: Judge whether the item flags its own jokeness: asking permission to tell a joke, labeling the form ('that's a play on words', 'all I need is a good one-liner'), or glossing the mechanism immediately after delivery. 10 = the frame speaks over the gag — the item announces and/or explains itself instead of performing. 5 = a light meta tag that does not crowd the punchline. 0 = the item performs with no meta-commentary. Reverse-scored: announcing deflates.
proposals.rationale: R08 ('You wanna hear a joke? Read this aloud'), R30 ('That's a play on word') and R33 ('all I need is a good one liner' followed by a blank) are dense-low and card-high. The card reads the signposting as clarity; the dense signal treats it as the joke failing to happen — whereas R06 works precisely because its meta move is itself a confession, not a label.

proposals.name: Headline-dependence of the comic engine
proposals.instruction: Delete the news-specific proper nouns and current-event hooks from the item and judge what comic mechanism survives. 10 = nothing survives — the item is a date-stamped gesture at a headline, and recognition of the news item is the entire joke. 5 = a topical hook plus some independent turn. 0 = evergreen; no news dependency. Reverse-scored: 10 means the joke is rented, not owned.
proposals.rationale: R03 (0.284 vs 0.782), R11 (0.181 vs 0.715), R35 (0.030 vs 0.688) and R46 (0.437 vs 0.903) are card-high and dense-low, and each collapses without its headline. Dense-high political items survive the deletion test — R31 (0.787 vs 0.264) repurposes a slogan, R20 (0.847 vs 0.396) runs an inversion — so the card is over-crediting topical recognition itself.

proposals.name: Host-forum self-reference as subject matter
proposals.instruction: Score how much the item's subject matter is the host forum itself: explicit mentions of the venue or its rituals ('this sub', 'r/jokes', '/r/jokes', 'Reddit', 'front page', 'upvotes', 'reposting', 'karma') or premises that only make sense to readers of this specific forum. 0 = no community reference anywhere; 10 = the entire premise depends on the audience knowing this venue and its habits. Score presence and centrality of the reference only; do not judge whether the joke is funny, original or well made.
proposals.rationale: Mode 2. Meta items cluster on the dense-favoured side of this slice (R03 0.897/0.370; R07 0.805/0.323; R49 0.767/0.054; R54; R57 0.935/0.120). The conjectured parent is that a readership rewards jokes addressed to itself -- its rituals, its repost culture -- so in-group address predicts reception through identity and belonging, not through joke construction; a crowd-trained reader plausibly perceives this while a criterion bank cannot name it. Tagged mixed because insiders can also genuinely craft better-fitting meta-humor (R03's plagiarism gag).
proposals.upstream_parent: audience in-group identity / community embeddedness of the poster

proposals.name: Reception-management furniture: vote appeals, repost apologies
proposals.instruction: Score how much audience-management furniture surrounds the joke: apologies, disclaimers, predictions or pleas about the post's own fate that appear as quoted text in the item ('this joke won't get any upvotes', 'technically a repost', 'sorry if repost', 'first post', 'all I need is a good one-liner', self-flagellation like 'I'm a terrible person'). 0 = none; 10 = the framing is dominated by talk about the post's own fate rather than the joke. Score presence and share of the text only; this is not a quality judgement.
proposals.rationale: Mode 4 prior. The furniture carries no comedic payload itself yet tracks the disagreement in both directions: R30 (0.682/0.125) and R31 (0.696/0.112) on the dense-favoured side, R08 (0.207/0.921) and R29 (0.166/0.807) on the card-favoured side. The parent is a posting habit of apologising and predicting reception -- social positioning about the post, orthogonal to whether the joke inside works. Purely nuisance.

proposals.name: Stock-punchline position in the retelling chain
proposals.instruction: Score how recognisably the punchline is a pre-existing, widely circulated classic payload the audience is assumed to already know -- famous set-piece puns and riddle answers that have circulated for years (e.g., the 'super-calloused fragile mystic hexed by halitosis' chain-joke, 'a play on word(s)', 'it's snot', 'she loves me... not', the antennas/reception wedding joke). 0 = punchline appears newly minted for this post; 10 = verbatim or near-verbatim retelling of a canonical joke. Score recognisable retelling status only; do not judge how well it is told or whether it is funny.
proposals.rationale: Mode 3. Every recognisable classic in the slice sits card-favoured: R27 (0.056/0.688), R34 (0.493/0.955), R38 (0.123/0.675), R39 (0.075/0.716), R50 (0.276/0.734), R17 (0.104/0.799) -- and R39 and R50 are the same canonical punchline retold with different framing, direct evidence of a retelling chain inside the slice. The scorecard rewards the intact classic mechanism; the crowd-faithful model plausibly encodes seen-it fatigue. Prior exposure is history about the joke, not craft in this text; tagged mixed because familiarity also genuinely dulls surprise.
proposals.upstream_parent: position in the retelling chain of a previously circulated joke (nth re-post)

proposals.name: Dated news pegs and era-bound platform idiom
proposals.instruction: Score how tightly the text is pegged to a passing moment: named public figures in a transient configuration, event pegs that decay within weeks, or era-bound internet idiom (e.g., 'one weird trick' clickbait formulas, a then-current app or subreddit, 'before the end of the decade', a named flood or election matchup). 0 = no datable peg, timeless; 10 = entirely dependent on this week's news or platform fashion. Score only the presence and perishability of the time peg; do not judge the joke's quality or its politics.
proposals.rationale: Modes 2/3. The card-favoured half is dense with perishable pegs: R56 (0.181/0.715, Clinton/Trump), R51 (0.284/0.782, Lewinsky/Bernie), R35 (0.437/0.903, Houston rain), R59 (0.187/0.868, end of decade), R16 (0.379/0.909, 'one weird trick'); era idiom also appears dense-favoured at R28 (0.787/0.264). The parent is submission timing: news-cycle heat and platform fashion rise and fall on their own calendar, so the peg predicts circulation through timeliness rather than construction. Tagged mixed because fresh shared context can also genuinely sharpen a joke.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission timing within the news cycle and forum era

proposals.name: Load-bearing taboo and shock register
proposals.instruction: Score how much the item's engine is charged content: mockery of groups or tragedies, terror or atrocity references, sexual or scatological explicitness, slur-adjacent stereotype framing. 0 = no charged content; 10 = transgression is the entire premise, with no other mechanism present. Score only the extent and load-bearing role of charged content; do not judge acceptability, taste or funniness.
proposals.rationale: Mode 4 prior. Charged engines appear on both sides: dense-favoured R01 (0.746/0.213), R40 (0.719/0.139), R53 (0.876/0.159), R58 (0.726/0.259); card-favoured R04 (0.170/0.683), R25 (0.319/0.914). The conjectured parent is controversy-driven engagement -- charged items mobilise both amused and outraged readers, so chargedness predicts circulation through provocation rather than through joke mechanics. Tagged mixed because transgression is also a genuine humor channel for this readership.
proposals.upstream_parent: controversy-driven engagement dynamics (mobilisation of opposing readers)

proposals.name: Cross-platform paste typography
proposals.instruction: Score how much typography indicates the text was composed elsewhere and pasted in: curly quotes and apostrophes, verse-citation or reference markers, bold/italic markup typical of another platform, preserved headline-style capitalisation, stray doubled line breaks or duplicated sentences from another layout. 0 = looks typed natively in the venue's plain text box; 10 = heavily imported formatting. Score only typographic evidence of pasting; this is not a quality judgement.
proposals.rationale: Mode 2 fingerprint of cross-platform sourcing. R57 carries scripture-app artifacts (verse markers, curly quotes) at 0.935/0.120; R46 and R45 carry smart apostrophes at 0.803/0.181 and 0.786/0.171; R02 carries foreign bold/italic markup at 0.636/0.165; R36 shows imported asterisk-italics on the card-favoured side (0.272/0.843). The marks index where the text was made, not how the joke is built; tagged mixed because content that already circulated elsewhere was survivorship-vetted for funniness.
proposals.upstream_parent: sourcing: composed or copied on another site/app and pasted into the venue

proposals.name: Truncation, spam and placeholder artifacts
proposals.instruction: Score how much of the text is non-authorial artifact rather than an intact joke: sentences cut off mid-thought, a setup with no punchline slot at all, SEO or spam strings, placeholder blanks standing in for a punchline, or content that is not a joke. 0 = complete, intact authored text; 10 = mostly artifact. Score textual integrity only; do not judge whether the joke would have been funny.
proposals.rationale: Mode 2. R24 is a sentence that stops at 'A man phones his work and says' yet sits dense-favoured (0.589/0.103); R48 is SEO spam text (0.487/0.012); R29's punchline is a blank rule '____________' (0.166/0.807). These are truncation, spam-bot and placeholder traces from the collection pipeline -- nothing authorial, nothing comedic. Purely nuisance: the parent cannot plausibly cause funniness.
proposals.upstream_parent: corpus assembly and automation artifacts (scraping truncation, spam bots)

proposals.name: Raw length and build verbosity
proposals.instruction: Score raw length from first word to last, including any title line: 0-2 = a single short line; 3-4 = one or two sentences; 5-6 = several sentences or short dialogue; 7-8 = a full paragraph or multi-part build; 9-10 = extended narrative or a long quoted block. Measure extent only; do not judge pacing, economy, or any other quality.
proposals.rationale: Mode 1. Length separates the halves of this slice: the card-favoured items are the long builds -- R36 (0.272/0.843), R39 (0.075/0.716), R50 (0.276/0.734) -- while many dense-favoured items are minimal one-liners like R06 (0.694/0.132), R19 (0.830/0.203) and R30 (0.682/0.125). Word count is the classic verbosity proxy: criterion banks reward development and completeness while readers reward economy, so raw length predicts model behaviour without being about funniness at all.

proposals.name: Title-plus-body submission scaffolding
proposals.instruction: Score how far the item uses the venue's two-part post structure: a short standalone title or label line (e.g., 'Old School Friend', 'Reddit Addiction', 'Super Hero jokes', 'Ghandi', 'Macbeth.docx') set off from a separate body. 0 = one continuous unit with no separate title; 10 = fully separate title plus a multi-paragraph body. Score layout structure only; this is not a quality judgement.
proposals.rationale: Modes 1/4. Titled posts skew card-favoured: R15 (0.261/0.811), R27 (0.056/0.688), R36 (0.272/0.843), R39 (0.075/0.716), R50 (0.276/0.734), with R49 (0.767/0.054) the slice's exception. The two-part structure is the visible fingerprint of a practiced submitter comfortable using the venue's full format -- a habit and seniority signal, not a property of the payload. Tagged mixed because practice plausibly also improves the joke itself.
proposals.upstream_parent: poster's practice with the venue's submission format

proposals.name: Verbatim borrowed canonical text as payload
proposals.instruction: Score how much verbatim, externally recognisable text the item embeds as its payload -- song lyrics quoted as the punchline, scripture passages, famous advertising or clickbait headline formulas, well-known movie or slogan lines -- where recognising the borrowed source is the point. 0 = every word appears written for this post; 10 = the joke is mostly quoted canonical text. Score only extent of verbatim borrowing; do not judge cleverness or funniness.
proposals.rationale: Mode 4 prior. Quoted canonical payloads split the models sharply: R46 embeds Rick Astley lyrics (0.803/0.181) and R57 quotes Ecclesiastes (0.935/0.120), both dense-favoured, while R16 recites the 'one weird trick' ad formula (0.379/0.909) and R60 lands on Monkees lyrics (0.250/0.851), both card-favoured. The parent is a recognition economy -- the audience's delight at catching a borrowed text -- which is a circulation effect, not construction. Tagged mixed because a well-timed recognition twist can genuinely land.
